faq.q: What's the difference between Median-cut and K-means?
faq.a: Both quantise the image into a set of colours but behave differently: median-cut keeps distinct colours, which suits pulling separate brand colours out of a logo; k-means averages pixels into smoother, blended tones. The palette presets choose for you — Brand (5, median-cut), Website (8, median-cut), Duotone (3), Gradient (4, k-means) and Detailed (12, k-means) — or set colours (3–16) and method yourself.

faq.q: Why doesn't an extracted colour appear in my photo?
faq.a: Because each reported colour is the average (centre) of a cluster of similar pixels, that average may not exist as any actual pixel. It also means the colour count changes the result, and extraction ranks by pixel area — so the top colour is often the background (sky, wall), not the accent you liked. Crop to the part you want before extracting, or click a specific point on the image.

faq.q: Can I pick an exact colour from one spot in the image?
faq.a: Yes. Click any point on the shown image and it reads that pixel, shows a zoomed magnifier preview and the hex, and adds it to a 'Picked Points' list. Each swatch displays hex, RGB, HSL, the nearest CSS colour name and its percentage share, and clicking copies it.

faq.q: How can I export the palette for code?
faq.a: Copy all HEX or all RGB, or use the export buttons for CSS variables, SCSS, JSON, an Adobe-style .aco text file, or a PNG strip image. 'Export all formats (ZIP)' bundles CSS, SCSS, JSON, an .aco text file, a plain hex list, the PNG strip and a README via JSZip. Saved palettes (up to 12) and your colour count/method persist in your browser. Keyboard: 1–9 copy a swatch, C copy all, S save, P download strip.
